articles.title: As ‘American Idol’ Leaves Los Angeles for Atlanta, More Concerns Emerge About the State of Local Production
articles.summary: Forget Hollywood. “American Idol” is heading to Georgia, dawg. In news that felt all too depressingly common in production-starved Los Angeles, word emerged Tuesday that “American Idol” — which has been broadcast live from Los Angeles since it originated in 2002 — would move production to Georgia.
body: The loss of more reality and game series production in California comes even as the state’s film and television tax credit program has expanded to include unscripted fare. But there’s a catch: Those competition shows must have a budget of more than $1 million per episode. That makes it difficult to qualify, even for major shows like “American Idol.”

The California incentives still don’t include docuseries, talk shows or game shows. States like New Jersey and Georgia, on the other hand, don’t limit their incentives. Georgia’s tax incentives require a total production spend of $500,000, making it more attractive for shows like “American Idol.”
“American Idol” was broadcast from Television City in the Fairfax district for most of its run; it later shifted to Red Studios Hollywood.
Deadline was first with the news about “American Idol’s” move to Georgia.

articles.title: ‘Love of Your Life’ Review: Margaret Qualley Goes on a Pretty but Surface-Level Healing Journey
articles.summary: It would probably be glib to refer to “Love of Your Life” as “Grieve Pray Love.” Rachel Morrison’s film about COVID-era loss, recovery and renewal is serious in intent and earnest in execution, grounded by a performance of intelligence and emotional transparency by Margaret Qualley, and doesn’t…
body: Rachel Morrison's second film as director follows a young nurse, bereaved during the global pandemic, as she grieves, escapes and returns to herself.

None of this even remotely resembles real life, which makes Maya’s emotional recovery increasingly hard to map: We learn in passing that she’s somehow funding these extended, luxurious travels with a career segue into telehealth, and when her online therapist observes that “we’re really getting somewhere,” we just have to take her word for it. Cox’s script, meanwhile, trades increasingly in one-size-fits-all therapy speak, and despite Qualley’s natural sincerity as a performer, Maya seems steadily less specific a personality as the years pass.

Late in proceedings, “Love of Your Life” gets a welcome jolt of feeling and truth from a scene that reunites Maya with Ruth, beautifully played by Keener with all the shattered, visible exhaustion of a woman who hasn’t got to nurture her grief in the Algarve sun. As she unpacks her damage, frankly but no longer angrily, against the unphotogenic greige backdrop of her house’s timber siding, “Love of Your Life” finally reconnects with reality, and not a moment too soon.

articles.title: Chase Infiniti on TIFF Breakout ‘The Julia Set,’ Love Bombing and Music Video Stardom
articles.summary: “The Julia Set” has emerged as one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. In her feature debut, writer-director Niki Byrne crafted a perfect showcase for the talents of “One Battle After Another” breakout Chase Infiniti.
body: Niki Byrne: Everything I’ve done makes sense in reverse. I came back to California from Europe in 2018 and started working in L.A. I was writing quite a bit at that point, and I knew I wanted to write and direct. I took Martin Scorsese’s master class, where he said that if you’re going to be a director of any quality, you must take acting classes. So, I did and found it super valuable. I’ve worked in almost every department on a film set and found acting incredibly difficult.

NB: When acting is done poorly, it’s the easiest job on set. When it’s done well, it’s by far the hardest. I wrote this movie during [COVID] lockdown and came out with this sort of weird confessional script and linked arms with [my producers], and we went on the hunt for our Julia. Then this one walked into a coffee shop in Koreatown.

Chase Infiniti: Three years ago. I was a month into shooting “Presumed Innocent.” And you did “One Battle After Another” between then and now, crazy. One of the things that struck me about this performance is how restrained your character is – even in the face of serious abuse and mistreatment from people and systems.
points: “The Julia Set” has emerged as one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival.

articles.title: ‘This should be condemned by any thinking human’: film industry rallies behind NAZA directors
articles.summary: Backing comes after Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor were threatened with having their citizenship revoked and accused of treason. Film industry heavyweights across the globe have expressed solidarity with Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of documentary NAZA, who have…
body: NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym euphemistically used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. It includes interviews with 24 Israeli military or intelligence soldiers and officers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza, resulting in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.
The film builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and the Guardian between 2023 and 2025.

The 80-minute documentary won the special jury prize at this year’s Venice film festival on Saturday, after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. On Sunday, Israel’s culture minister, Miki Zohar, accused the directors of being willing to “harm their homeland in order to receive applause from antisemites around the world”.
“I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for treason against the state,” Zohar wrote on X.

articles.title: All support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour quit after Macklemore dropped
articles.summary: The star said he was not responsible for Macklemore being dropped from the line-up after he made pro-Palestinian statements on stage.
body: All of the remaining support acts on Ed Sheeran's US tour have quit, after the rapper Macklemore was dropped from the line-up for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage.
Among them were Finneas, the brother of pop star Billie Eilish, who said in a statement: "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed."
Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish band Lukas Graham also announced their departure. Irish folk band Beoga, who perform with Sheeran on stage every night, dropped out too.
The announcements came hours after Sheeran said he would not be drawn into a public debate over Gaza, and stressed he was not responsible for Macklemore being removed from the tour.

articles.title: Trump says Kennedy Center to close as court rules his name must stay off building
articles.summary: The Trump-appointed board was blocked from adding the inscription "Renovated and Restored by President Donald J. Trump".
body: The Kennedy Center board has voted to close the performing arts centre for two years, just as a US judge blocked it from adding President Donald Trump's name back to the building.
In May, the same judge ordered the removal of Trump's name and blocked its temporary closure for proposed renovations.
Trump announced the addition of his name to the institution, among other rebranding measures across the nation's capital, last year.
The judge's written order came less than an hour before the centre's board voted on the closure.

articles.title: The Debut review – Julianne Moore is a thrill in Jesse Eisenberg’s oddball comedy
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: riotous lead performance holds together third movie from actor turned film-maker, about a housewife who joins a local musical. Jesse Eisenberg’s last two directorial efforts – the prickly comedy When You Finish Saving the World and the slightly softer A Real Pain – are small…
body: The Debut is about a repressed housewife, Mona (Julianne Moore), who decides to audition for a role in a community theater production of a musical called Nosy Neighbors, one of those gassy Manhattan trifles that were so ubiquitous on Broadway a half century ago. Mona’s kids are about to fly the nest, and her husband barely seems to notice her when she’s standing right next to him. So why not have a little creative adventure?

From that setup, Eisenberg could have gone to the obvious place, staging a sweet dramedy about a humble act of artistic expression opening Mona’s eyes to all the possibility of life outside her little bubble. He does do that, in part, but he also wants to take things to a darker place. The film gradually morphs into a study of actorly obsession and vanity, as Mona takes the Stanislavksi-esque teachings of the play’s director, Jerry (Paul Giamatti, doing his wearily charming thing), to extremes perhaps not seen since Black Swan. That’s a clever idea: a director watching in horror as the monster he’s created threatens to lay waste to his production.

articles.title: Venice best actress winner says she signed on at Danish job centre days before her victory
articles.summary: Mathilde Arcel, who won the Volpi Cup on Saturday for her role in Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown, said job offers have now begun to arrive. The winner of this year’s best actress prize at the Venice film festival has revealed that she is on unemployment benefits and had to fly to back to…
body: On Saturday night, Danish actor Mathilde Arcel won the prestigious Volpi Cup for her first leading role in a feature film, May el-Toukhy’s post-second world war drama Woman Unknown, which also won the Golden Lion award for best film.
Jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal said the judges had been able to relax Venice rules around not awarding more than one prize per film because the vote for Arcel had been unanimous.

After her triumph, the 30-year-old actor revealed in interviews with Danish media that she had returned to Denmark after her film’s premiere to sign on at the job centre, as she is on unemployment benefits when not working on films. She then returned to the Lido after being told it would be wise to be present at the awards gala.
In the UK, actors’ trade union Equity said in a 2023 report that 63% of its members have been in receipt of social security at some point in their life.

articles.title: ‘Closing Night’ Review: Sarah Paulson and Naomi Watts Lead a Deluxe Cast in a Shrill Family Melodrama in Search of a Binding Tone
articles.summary: Dianne Wiest, Toby Wallace and Odessa A’zion flesh out the ensemble of actor Cody Fern’s first feature as director and co-writer, about a famed actress grappling with a dark secret in a time of crisis.
body: Sandra is in rehearsals for her Broadway return in Brecht’s Mother Courage — and therein lies the first clue to her festering secret — but the seasoned pro is having uncharacteristic trouble remembering her lines and motivation. Nonetheless, she sends out formal invitations to her estranged family to attend the play’s opening.

Her jittery sister April ( Naomi Watts ) bristles at being “summoned” to a reunion after three decades of silence. But she can’t get there fast enough, concerned that her rudderless son Theo ( Toby Wallace ), who’s living in New York, should be kept away from his self-absorbed aunt. Before April can run interference, Theo drops a bombshell by revealing that he has already connected with the black-sheep diva. The scowling posters of Aunt Sandra all over town suggest that encounter was all but preordained.

April and Sandra’s tart-tongued, boozing mother Diane ( Dianne Wiest, in brilliant form) takes a hard pass on the trip from their distant hometown, where she owns a shabby hair salon. But once April starts reporting back, the blowzy old woman — still pissed about Sandra sleeping with April’s boyfriend when she was 15 — hops on a plane.

articles.title: Turner Prize winner's new vision for hometown
articles.summary: Keith Tyson said he hopes to create a space for exhibitions, education and community engagement.
body: A Turner Prize-winning artist has revealed plans to transform a former car showroom near where he grew up, into a centre for art and learning.
The privately funded project aims to give young people opportunities to experience art after Tyson's own artistic education was shaped by local libraries growing up.
He said "there were no galleries for miles around" so he thought this could be a chance to "give young people in the community an opportunity to see and learn about art" in a way that he never had.
Tyson said the project was still in its early stages but he was "excited by the building's potential to become an arts destination" for the north.
